assessment.overall_rationale: The two sets contain three strongly corresponding biological programs—bile acid/steroid conjugation, peroxisomal lipid metabolism, and sulfur/nitrogen metabolism—with only modest differences in scope and mechanistic emphasis.

pair_scores.rationale: Both describe the same hepatic SULT2A/GSTA3-centered bile acid, hydroxysteroid, and xenobiotic conjugation program, although the right module narrows the broader Nrf2/CAR-regulated Phase I/II scope.

The modules share hepatic detoxification, aldehyde handling, Cyb5b, and lipid-related context, but the right module centers on fatty acid oxidation and lipid storage rather than xenobiotic and steroid conjugation.
Bile acid regulation and general hepatic metabolic homeostasis provide limited context overlap, but sulfur and nitrogen catabolism is mechanistically distinct from Phase I/II detoxification.
Both include hepatic aldehyde or lipid-associated metabolism, but sulfation and xenobiotic conjugation differ fundamentally from peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation and lipid-droplet partitioning.
Both define essentially the same Hao2/Aldh3a2/Fitm1-centered program coupling peroxisomal fatty acid catabolism and fatty-aldehyde clearance to lipid-droplet homeostasis.
The modules share only broad hepatocyte metabolic and stress-homeostasis context, with little overlap between lipid oxidation and sulfur, nitrogen, or carbohydrate catabolism.
Their connection is largely through hepatic bile acid and sterol homeostasis, while cysteine and nitrogen catabolism differs from direct bile acid and steroid sulfation.
Both concern hepatocyte metabolic homeostasis, but sulfur and nitrogen handling has little mechanistic overlap with peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation and lipid storage.
Both describe the same Cdo1-centered hepatic sulfur and nitrogen metabolic program linked to taurine production, urea-cycle support, glucose regulation, and an aging hepatocyte signature.
